{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABXVWa7w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhA5Is4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 17, "title": "Add default 2D TextureNode round-trip support to loader and exporter", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 loader and exporter plugins currently reject ordinary `TextureNode` instances by default. As a result, a typical Three.js TSL material such as `material.colorNode = texture(myTexture)` cannot round-trip without custom paired adapters. 2D texture support is essential for practical TSL materials.

Extend the **existing** loader/exporter plugins to support ordinary 2D texture nodes, keeping the Three.js-first, minimal-implementation design. Use the extension's existing `$refTex` link to `glTF.textures[n]`, and delegate sampling/shader behavior to Three.js.

## Expected outcome

- Add **paired default serialization and resolution** for **2D `TextureNode`**, including the texture resource through the exporter writer and loader parser. Preserve graph node identity/shared texture references, material entrypoints, and standard glTF fallback.
- Preserve the relevant 2D sampling state and behavior supported by the chosen scope: explicit/default UV nodes, UV set/channel selection, texture UV transformations (offset/repeat/rotation/matrix, and their update behavior), sampler settings, color-space handling, mip level/bias and other common sampling options **when representable**. Audit the actual Three.js r186 `TextureNode` properties and implementation rather than assuming `serialize()` alone captures everything.
- Inspect how GLTFExporter/GLTFLoader represent textures and `KHR_texture_transform` and ensure that the TSL texture graph and ordinary glTF material properties remain correct together, without double-applying transformations or silently losing sampler/texture metadata.
- Where straightforward, also implement and test **`TextureSizeNode`** and **`MaxMipLevelNode`** for ordinary 2D textures.
- Explicitly decide, test and document the supported 2D sampling subset. Do **not** force support for features with unresolved glTF representation or runtime semantics (e.g., depth comparison, gather, gradients, mutable external references, advanced texture variants). Unsupported variants must fail explicitly on export, and failed material graph reconstruction on import must leave the entire ordinary glTF material fallback intact.
- Do not include `CubeTextureNode`, `Texture3DNode`, storage textures, renderer-owned textures/render targets, arbitrary live object references, or custom texture implementations in the required scope. Document the remaining limitations and adapter paths.
- Favor Three.js's own texture resource handling, `serialize()`/`deserialize()`, and node child discovery where suitable. Avoid duplicating shader semantics, embedding executable shader code, or unnecessarily changing the Draft v2.0 specification.

## Context

- [Draft v2.0 spec](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md) already defines `$refTex`.
- [TSL coverage matrix](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md) documents texture limitations.
- [Default exporter serializer](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/defaultNodeSerializer.ts)
- [Default loader resolver](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/defaultNodeResolver.ts)
- [Existing integration suite](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/demo/test/roundtrip.test.js)
- [Three.js r186 TextureNode implementation](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/TextureNode.js)
- Related coverage issue: #15 / PR #16.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Typical `texture(myTexture)` material entrypoints export and import by default, without consumer-defined adapters, through real GLTFExporter/GLTFLoader.
- [ ] Real 2D texture data and references survive repeated export → import → export → import cycles, with correct node graph links, shared references and applicable texture settings.
- [ ] Automated tests cover explicit/default UVs, UV channel selection and transformations, color space, sampler/mipmap behavior, and common 2D texture sampling options within the documented supported subset.
- [ ] Add tests for ordinary glTF core/KHR material properties coexisting with TSL texture nodes, including ordinary fallback in consumers without this extension.
- [ ] Validate unsupported modes/resources and malformed texture links; no silent graph loss, no partial TSL material application.
- [ ] Add `TextureSizeNode` and `MaxMipLevelNode` where compatible with the same constrained 2D resource model, or document precise blockers if not practical.
- [ ] Update the coverage matrix and package docs with what works by default, what requires adapters, and what remains deliberately unsupported.
- [ ] Preserve Draft v2.0-only behavior and the Three.js-first/minimal-implementation approach. Do not add Draft v1.0 compatibility.
- [ ] Run `npm --prefix packages/demo test`, builds for loader/exporter/demo, demo typecheck, and `git diff --check`. Report actual results and skipped checks.

## Optional validation

Run browser/WebGPU visual smoke tests for a textured material (UV transformations, sampled colors, normal-map usage if relevant to the supported scope). If not run, clearly report that Node-based tests do not prove GPU pixel correctness.

## Required post-merge verification
